blocks.text: The module contract explains supported OpenAI-compatible providers, thread-to-event-loop streaming, tool-call assembly, text-call salvage, Groq rescue, and cooldown rules. It also states what this adapter deliberately leaves to the loop and ledger.
blocks.title: Adapter contract and provider policy

blocks.text: Imports define the neutral model protocol and error types. Small helpers lazily load llm_client, read SDK objects or mappings, convert tool and message shapes, normalize Mistral call ids, and extract cached or streamed usage.
blocks.title: Request and usage conversion

blocks.text: _Holdback delays prefixes that might be textual tool-call markup. It releases ordinary text promptly, switches to holding when a marker is found, and retains undecided suffixes until more input arrives.
blocks.title: Holding possible text calls

blocks.text: _StreamState records text, usage, finish reason, and interleaved tool fragments. At stream completion it emits held text, native or salvaged ToolCall values, and a Usage event, including explicit errors for unsafe arguments.
blocks.title: Neutralizing one provider stream

blocks.text: Endpoint resolves a supplied client, a base URL client, or a configured repository factory. It skips cooling keys and records authentication or rate-limit cooldowns without allowing bookkeeping failures to fail the model call.
blocks.title: Endpoint construction and cooldowns

blocks.text: The adapter validates endpoint configuration, creates request kwargs, and tries endpoints in order. Each endpoint runs its synchronous SDK stream in a daemon worker, transfers chunks through an asyncio queue, classifies failures, and closes the underlying network stream on cancellation or completion.
blocks.title: Endpoint fallback and cancellation

purpose: This adapter connects the agent model protocol to OpenAI-style chat completion APIs. It supports provider chains, cooldown-aware endpoint selection, native and text-salvaged tool calls, usage reporting, and cancellation of synchronous SDK streams.
summary: Streams OpenAI-compatible model responses and converts provider-specific chunks into neutral text, tool-call, and usage events.
